project.name: FlatBuffers
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/flatbuffers` is on commit `8fb8c2ce1dff00bc1455aba0770eb7eae9a06ece`, not metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The packaged `patch.diff` adds unrelated `--cs-global-alias` support and does not touch `include/flatbuffers/util.h` or the empty-input parser path in `src/idl_parser.cpp`, so the line anchors and causal chain below are grounded on the staged vulnerable source plus `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `reproduction_report.json`, not on that patch artifact.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502006 (flatbuffers): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target parser_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502006
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 3-byte file `20 20 20`. `flatbuffers_parser_fuzzer` requires `size >= 3`, discards the first two bytes as control fields, and therefore passes the one-byte C string `" "` into `flatbuffers::Parser::Parse()`. `Parser::Next()` skips that lone space and then returns `kTokenEof`, so `StartParseFile()` immediately executes `Error("input file is empty")`. `Parser::Message()` formats that error with `NumToString(line_)` and `NumToString(CursorPosition())`; on this path both integers are 1 because `ResetState()` / `MarkNewLine()` set `line_` to 1 and `Next()` leaves `cursor_` one byte past the only space. The saved MemorySanitizer trace does not attribute the poison to those parser integers. Instead it states that the uninitialized value was created by allocation of local `ss` in `flatbuffers::NumToString<int>`, and the first project frame on the crash stack is `ss << t` in `include/flatbuffers/util.h:130`. The packaged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated to this parser/error-formatting path, so the chain below is grounded on the staged vulnerable source and the saved MSan origin rather than on a matching fix hunk.

source.description: First project statement that materializes the whitespace-only parser body as EOF state. After the harness strips the first two bytes from `20 20 20`, `Next()` skips the single remaining space and then sets `token_ = kTokenEof`, which is the state `StartParseFile()` immediately uses to enter the empty-input error path.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is three ASCII spaces. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` drops bytes 0 and 1, constructs `input` from the remainder, and passes `parse_input = input.c_str()` to `parser.Parse()` at `tests/fuzzer/flatbuffers_parser_fuzzer.cc:47`. For this witness the parser body is exactly one space byte followed by the C-string terminator.

sink.description: Project sink. Formatting the already-defined integer argument through local `std::stringstream ss` reaches the saved MemorySanitizer crash in libc++ `std::__1::basic_stringbuf::overflow(int)`.
sink.note: The saved stack's first project frame is `flatbuffers::NumToString<int>` at `include/flatbuffers/util.h:130`, immediately below libc++ `overflow`, `xsputn`, and `operator<<(int)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `NumToString` stack-allocates local stream object `ss`, and the saved MemorySanitizer origin says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `ss` in this function's stack frame.
root_cause.note: The parser-side values being formatted are defined on the witnessed path (`line_ == 1`, `CursorPosition() == 1`). The saved MSan origin instead points to local `ss` inside `NumToString<int>`, so the uninitialized bytes are grounded at this stack object rather than in parser state.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer attributes the poisoned value to stack allocation of `ss` in `flatbuffers::NumToString<int>`. On the witnessed path this is the concrete local object later consumed by `ss << t`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 3-byte witness satisfies `size >= 3`. After the harness strips the first two bytes, it passes the single-space C string `" "` into `Parser::Parse()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness strips the first two bytes from the three-space witness and passes the remaining one-byte parser body `" "` into `Parser::Parse()`.
The lexer skips the lone space, materializes `kTokenEof`, and `StartParseFile()` immediately takes the `input file is empty` error path.
The error formatter converts `line_` and `CursorPosition()` to strings with `NumToString`; on this path both values are 1.
Each `NumToString(1)` call allocates stack local `std::stringstream ss`, and `ss << t` reaches the saved MSan use-of-uninitialized-value in libc++ `basic_stringbuf::overflow`.

fine_trace.note: Source. After the harness reduces the witness to the single parser byte `" "`, `Next()` first takes the whitespace case for that space and loops. The following `\0` case then backs `cursor_` to the terminator and materializes `token_ = kTokenEof`, which is the parser state that drives the empty-input error path.

fine_trace.code: if (Is(kTokenEof)) return Error("input file is empty");
fine_trace.note: Because step 1 produced EOF from the whitespace-only parser body, `StartParseFile()` does not enter declaration parsing and instead calls `Error("input file is empty")` immediately.

The gcc-style error formatter converts the current line number and cursor offset to strings. On this path `ResetState()` / `MarkNewLine()` made `line_ == 1`, and `Next()` left `cursor_` one byte past the single space so `CursorPosition() == 1`; the saved MSan origin is therefore not these integers, but the local stream allocated inside `NumToString`.

Root cause. Each `NumToString(1)` call on step 3 stack-allocates local stream object `ss`. The saved MemorySanitizer origin explicitly says `Uninitialized value was created by an allocation of 'ss' in the stack frame` of `flatbuffers::NumToString<int>`.

Sink. Inserting the defined integer argument (`t == 1` on the witnessed path) into step 4's local stream reaches libc++ `std::__1::basic_stringbuf::overflow(int)` / `xsputn`, where the saved MemorySanitizer report fires.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan origin says `Uninitialized value was created by an allocation of 'ss' in the stack frame` of `flatbuffers::NumToString<int>` at `include/flatbuffers/util.h:125`; the concrete local object is `std::stringstream ss;` at line 129.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved MSan trace executes `/out/parser_fuzzer /tmp/poc` and reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` through `flatbuffers::NumToString<int>` on the empty-input error path.

format.name: 3-byte flatbuffers parser_fuzzer input
format.contract: The saved evidence proves the exact 3-byte witness `20 20 20`. In this witness the harness ignores the first two bytes and passes the exact one-byte parser body `" "` to `Parser::Parse()`. The trigger semantics are specifically that `Next()` skips that lone space, returns `kTokenEof`, and `StartParseFile()` reports `input file is empty`, which makes `Message()` call `NumToString(1)` and `NumToString(1)`. The staged artifacts do not prove a broader whitespace class or a matching fix.
